mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate level predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as it reduces the cost of capital for corporations and increases the present value of future cash flows.
failure_condition: Rank IC for FEDFUNDS and 20-day S&P 500 returns remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or the average 20-day return when FEDFUNDS is below 1.0% is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 3.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, leading to reduced corporate earnings expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the 5-day windows following UNRATE > 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous month-over-month increase in retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 0.5% signals robust consumer and housing demand, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and HOUST both increase > 0.5% MoM
failure_condition: The average 60-day S&P 500 return following periods where RSAFS and HOUST both increase by more than 0.5% MoM is negative, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 2.5% YoY), the expectation of monetary policy tightening reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the 20-day windows following CPIAUCSL > 2.5% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 1.0% signals an impending monetary tightening cycle, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the 5-day windows following FEDFUNDS > 1.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A rising payroll employment level (PAYEMS) indicates a strengthening labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 20-day S&P 500 return following PAYEMS increases is negative, or the Rank IC for PAYEMS (MoM change) and 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A housing starts level below 1700.0 thousand units signals a weakening housing market, which reduces consumer confidence and corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the 5-day windows following HOUST < 1700.0.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and GDP (GDPC1) signals a deepening economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 60-day S&P 500 return following periods where INDPRO < 105.0 and GDPC1 < 19700.0 is positive, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
